scope: Initial upload/batch creation acknowledgement, durable rejection tombstones, optional expected-owner admission and transaction races

verified_invariants.name: Creation admission is atomic
verified_invariants.conclusion: BEGIN IMMEDIATE covers rejected/accepted-key lookup, validation, quota admission, every new draft/batch/session row and saved acknowledgement on one connection. Exceptions unwind the connection transaction before rejection handling.

verified_invariants.name: Confirmed rejection cannot race a later same-key creation
verified_invariants.conclusion: The second BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction refuses to tombstone an accepted key. Otherwise the tombstone commits before a rejection header is emitted, and later creation checks the tombstone under the same serialized write admission.

verified_invariants.name: Schema and application 4xx rejection share the same durable proof
verified_invariants.conclusion: The custom APIRoute handles RequestValidationError and HTTPException only for the two creation POST paths. It emits the exact-key rejection marker only after reject returns following a successful transaction exit. Existing accepted keys, invalid/duplicate keys, expected-owner mismatch and 5xx exceptions do not receive this proof.

verified_invariants.name: Owner binding precedes creation and rejection
verified_invariants.conclusion: When supplied, one Upload-Creation-Owner value must exactly equal authenticated current_owner. Both normal handlers and the schema-error wrapper enforce this before admitting or retiring the key. Duplicate and mismatched owner values fail without a rejection marker.

verified_invariants.name: Canonicalization and replay preserve original admission
verified_invariants.conclusion: Validated Pydantic model dumps with sorted JSON keys bind payloads, including typed defaults. Matching accepted keys bypass new quota/draft admission and return owner-scoped current sessions in the saved order. Different payloads or creation kinds cannot reuse an accepted key.

limits: This is static inspection of the pinned files, not an independently executed concurrency or HTTP/browser test.
Expected-owner binding is optional for API compatibility; clients omitting that header use the authenticated request owner.
Different idempotency keys remain distinct requests. Browser storage failure and cross-tab intent coordination are client concerns outside this backend-only closure.
No power-loss, actual deployment, model qualification, long-match capacity or live-system claim is made.
